summary: SelectAvailability: Availability Ids Never Expire: Ids Over 100 Minutes Old Are Accepted by SelectAvailability and Passed to the Supplier by NextAvailability (also: TC-NEXTAVAIL-EDGE-05)
spec_ref: Round 3 Select edge case 10, NextAvailability edge case 05 (id lifetime is UNKNOWN in SPEC)
expected_value: A 4xx "availability search expired" answer (with a documented lifetime) from both calls.
impact: Callers cannot tell a stale search from a live one; FareConfirm is the only point where the staleness shows.
evidence: First-page ids captured about 108 minutes earlier are still accepted: SelectAvailability returns HTTP 200 with an offerId, and NextAvailability forwards the stale pointer to the supplier, which times out (HTTP 409 Z9999 "Request Timed Out or Canceled" with OriginalSupplierRequest). No "expired" answer exists, so a stale search can be selected and priced long after the inventory it showed may be gone.
